chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu al-Nu'man al-Ijli, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

O Abu al-Nu'man! Do not let the people deceive you regarding yourself, for the matter will reach you through them, and do not pass your day with such and such, for there is with you one who preserves your deeds for you. And do good, for I have not seen anything that is better in attainment nor faster in seeking than a new good deed for an old sin.
A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from 'Uthman ibn Isa, from one of our companions, from Abu al-Nu'man — similar to it.
ai.seo_question: What is the best remedy for an old sin according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Baqir (AS) reassures Abu al-Nu'man that divine awareness transcends human perception, urging him not to be distracted by worldly opinions. He highlights the spiritual efficacy of 'new' good deeds as a rapid and potent expiation for past sins, a concept central to Shia theology regarding the fluidity of spiritual status. This teaching underscores the dynamic nature of repentance, where immediate action can swiftly rectify previous shortcomings.
